title: Which? - welch-
sourceNote: The transcript is garbled, especially the example sentences. The examples below keep the teacher's structure (nominative, accusative, dative for all genders and the plural) in standard German.
objectives: I can ask about something specific with *welch-* (which)
I can choose the correct ending of *welch-* for gender, case and plural
I can answer a *welch-* question with the definite article
I can use *welch-* after prepositions like *mit*, *zu*, *von*

expressions.de: Zu welchem Hut passt meine Jacke?
expressions.en: Which hat goes with my jacket?
Which woman are you talking to?

patterns.ex: Mit welchem Buch lernst du Deutsch?
patterns.en: Which book do you learn German with?

grammar.title: When to use welch-
grammar.body:
Use **welch-** when you ask about something **particular** out of several (which one?). The ending depends on the **article of the noun** and the **case**. In fact the endings of *welch-* are the same as the endings of the definite article **der / die / das**: welch- takes the last letters of the article.

The answer normally uses the **definite article** (der, die, das), because you mean a specific thing.
grammar.ar: welch- = أيّ؟ وتأخذ نهاية أداة التعريف نفسها (der → welcher، den → welchen ...).

examples.de: Welcher Hut ist schön? - Der Hut dort.
examples.en: Which hat is nice? - That hat there.

grammar.title: All forms of welch-
grammar.body: Compare with the definite article: **der → welcher**, **den → welchen**, **dem → welchem**, **die → welche**, **der → welcher**, **das → welches**, **den → welchen**.
grammar.ar: المؤنث والجمع في المرفوع والمنصوب: welche. المفعول غير المباشر: welchem / welcher / welchem / welchen.

grammar.title: Masculine: welcher / welchen / welchem
grammar.body: In the nominative **der Hut** becomes **welcher Hut**. In the accusative (after verbs like *kaufen*, *finden*) **den Hut** becomes **welchen Hut**. In the dative (after *mit*, *zu*, *von*, *bei* ...) **dem Hut** becomes **welchem Hut**.

examples.de: Welcher Hut ist schön? - Der Hut dort.
examples.en: Which hat is nice? - That hat there.

examples.de: Welchen Hut findest du schön? - Den Hut dort.
examples.en: Which hat do you think is nice? - That hat there.

examples.de: Zu welchem Hut passt meine Jacke? - Zu dem Hut dort.
examples.en: Which hat goes with my jacket? - With that hat there.

grammar.title: Feminine: welche / welche / welcher
grammar.body: The feminine article **die** does not change in the nominative and accusative, so it is **welche** in both. After a dative preposition **der Frau** becomes **welcher Frau**.

examples.de: Welche Frau ist deine Kollegin? - Die Frau dort.
examples.en: Which woman is your colleague? - That woman there.

examples.de: Welche Frau kennst du? - Die Frau dort.
examples.en: Which woman do you know? - That woman there.

examples.de: Mit welcher Frau sprichst du? - Mit der Frau dort.
examples.en: Which woman are you talking to? - To that woman there.

grammar.title: Neuter: welches / welches / welchem
grammar.body: **das Buch** gives **welches Buch** in the nominative and the accusative (the neuter article does not change). In the dative **dem Buch** gives **welchem Buch**, the same as masculine.

examples.de: Welches Buch ist interessant? - Das Buch hier.
examples.en: Which book is interesting? - This book here.

examples.de: Welches Buch liest du? - Das Buch hier.
examples.en: Which book are you reading? - This book here.

examples.de: Mit welchem Buch lernst du Deutsch? - Mit dem Buch hier.
examples.en: Which book do you learn German with? - With this book here.

grammar.title: Plural: welche / welche / welchen
grammar.body: The plural article **die** gives **welche** in the nominative and the accusative. In the dative **den** gives **welchen**, and the noun gets an extra **-n**, unless it already ends in *-n*: **den Blumen**, but **den Kindern**.

examples.de: Welche Blumen sind schön? - Die Blumen dort.
examples.en: Which flowers are beautiful? - The flowers there.

examples.de: Welche Blumen kaufst du? - Die Blumen dort.
examples.en: Which flowers are you buying? - The flowers there.

examples.de: Von welchen Blumen sprichst du? - Von den Blumen dort.
examples.en: Which flowers are you talking about? - About the flowers there.
Which children are you playing with?

mistakes.why: *Hut* is masculine and an accusative object: *welchen*.
*mit* needs the dative; feminine dative is *welcher*.

pronunciation.tip: Say 'velkh' with a soft *ch* at the end of the syllable, like a hiss: *welcher*.
The German *w* is pronounced like English 'v': *Welcher* = 'Vel-kher'.

tip: Find the case from the verb or the preposition first, then pick the same ending as the definite article: der Hut → welcher, den Hut → welchen, dem Hut → welchem.

comprehension.a: When you ask about something particular (which one?).

comprehension.q: What is the accusative masculine form?
What is the dative feminine form?
Which forms are the same in the nominative and accusative?
What happens to the noun in the dative plural?
comprehension.a: It gets an extra -n (den Blumen), unless it already ends in -n.

exercises.title: Question and answer
exercises.instructions: Choose the correct article for the answer.

items.q: Welchen Hut kaufst du? - ___ Hut dort. (Der / Den)
Welcher Hut ist schön? - ___ Hut dort. (Der / Den)
Mit welcher Frau sprichst du? - Mit ___ Frau dort. (der / die)
Welches Buch liest du? - ___ Buch hier. (Das / Dem)
Von welchem Buch sprichst du? - Von ___ Buch hier. (das / dem)
Welche Blumen kaufst du? - ___ Blumen dort. (Die / Den)

exercises.title: Word order
exercises.instructions: Put the words in the correct order.

items.q: Which hat do you want? (der Hut)
items.a: Welchen Hut möchtest du? / Welchen Hut willst du?

items.q: With which child do you play? (das Kind)

summary: Endings equal the definite article: **der → welcher, den → welchen, dem → welchem; die → welche, der → welcher; das → welches, dem → welchem**.
Answer with the definite article: **Welchen Hut? - Den Hut dort.**
